newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, Argentina delay signing mining treaty.
newsitem.headline: Chile, Argentina delay signing mining treaty.

text.p: Chile and Argentina have delayed signing a border mining treaty which was due to have been signed during a visit by Argentine President Carlos Menem to Chile this week, said a Chilean official.

Emilio Ruiz-Tagle, head of the South American department of the foreign ministry, said the agreement governing mining in border areas was not ready to be signed by Menem and his Chilean counterpart Eduardo Frei.

"It is a treaty to which both countries assign extraordinary importance as it will allow the exploitation of deposits in the Andes which, without the agreement, could simply not be exploited," said Ruiz-Tagle.
The two leaders are due to sign six accords during Menem's two-day visit including pacts on integrated border posts, forestry cooperation and help in the event of catastrophes.
Menem will arrive in Chile on Thursday to take part in the official opening of the GasAndes natural gas pipeline which will pump gas to Santiago from the Argentine city of Mendoza.
